title_index: Chatbot-Delivered Interventions for Improving Mental Health Among Young People: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
modality_delivery_raw: Chatbots delivered via instant messengers (n=14), mobile applications (n=10), web-based platforms (n=2), robots (n=2), and virtual reality (n=1). Interactions encompassed text-only (n=21), voice-only (n=1), written and spoken (n=4), spoken and visual (n=3), with synchronous two-way interactions. AI-based chatbots (n=20) and rule-based (n=10).
therapeutic_approach_raw: approaches: Integrative approach (n=12) and cognitive behavioral therapy (n=7) were most frequently utilized among 26 studies that incorporated theoretical frameworks. Also references to mindfulness-based stress reduction, acceptance commitment therapy, and psychoeducation across included studies.
dose_structure_raw: Duration varied significantly, ranging from a single session lasting 15 min to interventions spanning over 4 months. Most studies (n=20) had 2-4 week duration, with <1 week (n=4) and >4 weeks (n=5). Most chatbots deployed as standalone systems (n=25); 4 integrated as components within larger platforms.
architecture_raw: AI-based chatbots (n=20) using algorithms or neural networks to process natural language; rule-based chatbots (n=10) with predefined rules or decision trees. One study used both types. Review recommends integrating strengths of both approaches.
entry_channel_raw: Chatbots were delivered via instant messengers (n=14, e.g., Facebook, WeChat), mobile applications (n=10), web-based platforms (n=2), robots (n=2), and virtual reality (n=1). Instant messenger platforms were recommended for delivery as they can remove entry barriers and improve availability of mental health support.

modality_delivery_raw: LLM-based (GPT-4o) text generation of bystander intervention responses to cyberaggression scenarios. Three strategies compared: standard policy reminder (static text), baseline GPT (generic prompt), and AllyGPT (theory-driven prompt with decision tree). Text-only output; asynchronous generation against pre-collected examples rather than real-time user interaction.
therapeutic_approach_raw: approaches: Bystander intervention theory (Latané & Darley sequential model); 5 constructive intervention strategies: calling out aggressive behavior, correcting misinformation, validating and expressing empathy, advising disengagement, redirecting the discussion. Grounded in psychological literature on helping behavior, empathy, de-escalation, and social norms. | ssi_framing: False
dose_structure_raw: Single-response generation per cyberaggression scenario (not a multi-session intervention). For each of 1000 scenarios, one response is generated per strategy (3 strategies = 3000 total). AllyGPT uses a two-stage decision tree: (1) assess incivility level (low/moderate/high), (2) assess direction (group-targeted vs individual-targeted), then (3) select and combine strategies accordingly. The sequence is fixed/deterministic (decision tree), not user-selected or adaptive to user input.
architecture_raw: Hybrid orchestration: deterministic decision tree selects intervention strategies based on assessed incivility level and aggression direction; generative LLM (GPT-4o) then produces the actual response text. The decision logic is fixed (rule-based), while content generation is generative. Model autonomy is constrained by 'dos and don'ts' prompting guidelines for each strategy. No explicit guardrails beyond prompt design are described.

title_index: Systematic review and meta-analysis of AI-based conversational agents for promoting mental health and well-being. [Review]
modality_delivery_raw: AI-based conversational agents (CAs) / chatbots; retrieval-based (n=30) and generative (n=5); text-based (n=24) and multimodal/voice-based (n=11); delivered via smartphone/tablet apps (n=16), instant messengers (n=9), robots (n=5), web-based platforms (n=3), VR (n=1), EMDR platform (n=1); stand-alone (n=32) or integrated (n=3).
therapeutic_approach_raw: approaches: CBT (n=6); integrative approaches (n=11) including DBT, CBT, mindfulness, ACT, EFT, SFBT, motivational interviewing, IPT, self-compassion therapy, positive psychology; BA (n=2); MOL (n=3); person-centered therapy (n=1); transtheoretical model of change (n=1); NR (n=11). dose_structure_raw: Study duration varied considerably, from several minutes (e.g., 15 min, 20 min single sessions) to 6 months. Most CAs were stand-alone (n=32). Specific session structure, number of stages/agents, required vs optional components, and sequence adaptivity are not systematically reported at the review level.
architecture_raw: Two main response generation approaches: retrieval-based (n=30), which use dialog management frameworks to select responses from a pre-established repository; and generative (n=5), which use ML algorithms to auto-generate responses. Safety measures in 15 studies including automatic crisis/harm identification.

modality_delivery_raw: Across the 43 included studies, modalities included text-based chatbot/conversational interfaces (e.g., ChatGPT), question-and-answer interfaces, and classification/detection systems applied to social media text. Of 9 generative applications, 7 used the text-based ChatGPT user interface and 2 used text-based interfaces for an educational BERT model and a data-secure FLAN model. The review notes guardrails are needed: 'models of LLM use in crisis support contexts are most likely to be those that are driven by clinical oversight, with sufficient guardrails in place to trigger referrals when clinically indicated.'

title_index: A chatbot architecture for promoting youth resilience
modality_delivery_raw: Chatbot (rule-based dialog graph) delivered via Facebook Messenger on mobile phones; text-based dialog with avatars, media files (images, animated GIFs), and minigames; asynchronous interaction with daily engagement prompts
therapeutic_approach_raw: approaches: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and positive psychology; includes relaxation strategies, problem solving, recognizing and tackling negative thoughts, interpersonal and communication skills, gratitude journaling, scheduling positive activities | ssi_framing: False
dose_structure_raw: Headstrong: 4-week program with daily engagement, over 20 distinct activities each engaging the user for 5-10 minutes. 21-Day Stress Detox: 21 days, once per day engagement, daily check-in at chosen time, stress rating, new activity module each day, ending with choice of motivational quote, joke, or gratitude journal entry. Aroha: one-off user-driven engagement. Activity modules are unique per day; daily loop components re-used; some statements drawn randomly from pre-authored sets for variation.
architecture_raw: Rule-based (deterministic) dialog graph architecture with thousands of dialog nodes; uses Google Dialogflow for intent matching of user input. Visual authoring interface (CMS) creates directed graph structure with color-coded node types. Hybrid potential noted: authors discuss future integration of deep-learning-based dialog for rapport building and discovery while retaining crafted dialog for evidence-based activities. Content constraints include emergency escalation module for risk phrases.
entry_channel_raw: Facebook Messenger was selected as the front-end interface for the chatbot to engage young people with a familiar interface likely to be already installed on their phones. Users were recruited from two local secondary schools for field trials, and undergraduates were recruited from large classes for the 21-Day Stress Detox.

Suggested platforms: Google Dialogflow, IBM Watson Assistant, Amazon Lex, Wit.AI. Self-decision: classifier recommends a technique; user may accept, defer, or freely select an alternative. Advice provision: technique-specific guidance delivered. Users may accept or defer engagement without restriction.

title_index: Feasibility of the LvL UP digital lifestyle coaching intervention designed to prevent non-communicable diseases and common mental disorders.
modality_delivery_raw: Mobile app with rule-based conversational agent (chatbot), text-based interaction with minimal free-text input and pre-defined answer options, asynchronous interaction
dose_structure_raw: Intended to be used daily for 21 days with one coaching session per day, after which continued use is optional. Three levels with gamified progression through LvL UP Shield completion. Users can complete tasks across four categories: Coaching Sessions, Life Hacks, Tools (Breeze or Journal), and Basics. Users could view and edit journal entries at any time. Progress tracked via puzzle pieces filling the Shield; completing a shield unlocks a storytelling episode and progression to next level.
architecture_raw: Rule-based workflow-orchestrated system with scripted sessions and pre-defined answer options developed by domain experts. No natural language processing ability to ensure fidelity and safety of intervention content.
entry_channel_raw: Online recruitment leveraged various channels, including posts on Telegram groups dedicated to research participation, electronic direct mail (EDM) marketing and social media posts via the research centre's mailing list and social platforms, and ad campaigns through a dedicated LvL UP social media page. Social media ad campaigns on Meta and Google Ads began in March 2023 for iOS and expanded to both iOS and Android from May to July 2023. Offline efforts included door-to-door and on-street flyer distribution in residential areas, complemented by six student interns distributing flyers in high-footfall locations around the university campus over a 10-day period. Additionally, a referral link within the app enabled participants to invite friends and colleagues to download and engage with the app.
